text: Then it starts raining. And the entire soundscape changes. Drops strike pavement, metal, leaves, umbrellas, glass. Thousands of tiny impacts create new sounds across the environment. But rain doesn't simply reveal a perfect map. It can also drown out quieter echoes. Every environment has its own acoustic character. And learning to navigate with sound means learning when to trust a clue, when to check it, and when to slow down.
